item.text:
# Shehbaz Sharif, Pakistan (2024) - 1B.1 evidence note

Bounded web pass completed with multiple query formulations and no further searching. The 2024 record I found is mostly de-escalatory or defensive; I did not find strong 2024 evidence that Sharif personally sought nuclear or existential escalation for prestige or leverage.

| Polarity | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | Question IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Favorable | Pakistan's nuclear programme is for peaceful purposes: PM | Radio Pakistan | 2024-12-24 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/24-12-2024/pm-vows-to-root-out-scourge-of-terrorism | Sharif publicly framed Pakistan’s nuclear program as defensive and non-aggressive, saying it was for self-defense and had no aggressive designs. This is direct support for a risk-reduction reading. | 1B.1 |
| Favorable | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | In his UNGA address, Sharif urged India to enter dialogue for a peaceful resolution of Kashmir, which is consistent with reducing interstate risk rather than escalating toward war. | 1B.1 |
| Mixed | PM stresses for peaceful solution of global challenges | Radio Pakistan | 2024-09-27 | https://www.radio.gov.pk/27-09-2024/pm-urges-india-to-engage-in-dialogue-for-resolution-of-jk-dispute | The same speech also used hard-edged rhetoric, accusing India of military expansion and describing its war doctrine as operating under a nuclear overhang. That language is confrontational and can be read as leverage-seeking pressure, but it still stops short of a call for escalation by Pakistan. | 1B.1 |

## Search gap

- I found no strong 2024 primary-source or Reuters evidence that Sharif initiated nuclear brinkmanship, ordered escalation, or used existential-risk threats as a prestige/power tool.
- The closest 2024 material was defensive diplomacy and deterrent framing, not escalation behavior.
- Because the evidence base is sparse, confidence on 1B.1 should be limited to a mild favorable read rather than a strong one.
